verses.zh: （亚萨的诗，交与伶长。用迦特乐器。）你们当向　神―我们的力量大声欢呼，向雅各的　神发声欢乐！
verses.en: For the music director, according to the gittith style;[NOTE:1] by Asaph.Shout for joy to God, our source of strength!Shout out to the God of Jacob!
notes: Psalm 81. The psalmist calls God’s people to assemble for a festival and then proclaims God’s message to them. The divine speech (vv. 6-16) recalls how God delivered the people from Egypt, reminds Israel of their rebellious past, expresses God’s desire for his people to obey him, and promises divine protection in exchange for obedience.
verses.commentary:
81:1-5 This strophe is an admonition
of the psalmist to the covenant people to rejoice at YHWH's powerful deliverance
of Israel from Egyptian bondage.

- sing for joy ‒ BDB 943, KB 1247, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 32:11

- shout joyfully ‒ BDB 929, KB 1206, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- raise a song ‒ BDB 669, KB 724, Qal IMPERATIVE

- strike the timbrel ‒ BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERATIVE

- blow the trumpet ‒ BDB 1075, KB 1785, Qal IMPERATIVE

81:1 "to God our strength" "Strength" (BDB 738) is often linked with "refuge" (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: REFUGE)
to describe God (cf. Ps. 14:6; 46:1; 62:6-7). Faithful followers' hope, peace, and joy are in Him.

▣ "sing. . .shout" These were worship acts done in the temple on special gathering days.

▣ "the God of Jacob" This is an idiom for all the thirteen tribes of Israel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

"God" is Elohim. This is the most common designation of Israel's Deity in
Books 2 and 3 of the Psalter (i.e., Ps. 42-72; Ps. 73-89).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

verses.zh: 唱起诗歌，打手鼓，弹美琴与瑟。
verses.en: Sing[NOTE:1] a song and play the tambourine,the pleasant-sounding harp, and the ten-stringed instrument.
notes: The precise meaning of the Hebrew term הַגִּתִּית (haggittit) is uncertain; it probably refers to a musical style or instrument. See the superscription to Ps 8.
verses.commentary:
81:2 "the timbrel" This musical instrument (BDB 1074, KB 1771) was a small handheld, circular
frame with stretched animal skin. It was used in association with women dancing in the exodus victory
in Exod. 15:20 (also note Jdgs. 11:34; 1 Sam. 18:6).

▣ "lyre" This stringed musical instrument (BDB 490, KB 484) was used in many cultural settings.

▣ "harp" This musical instrument (BDB 614) has been identified in several ways (see notes at Psalm 150).

- harp

- lute

- guitar

verses.zh: 当在月朔并月望―我们过节的日期吹角，
verses.en: Sound the ram’s horn on the day of the new moon[NOTE:1] and on the day of the full moon when our festival[NOTE:2] begins.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “lift up.”

Heb “at the new moon.”sn New moon festivals were a monthly ritual in Israel (see R. de Vaux, Ancient Israel, 469-70). In this context the New Moon festival of the seventh month, when the Feast of Tabernacles was celebrated (note the reference to a “festival” in the next line), may be in view.

The festival in view is probably the Feast of Tabernacles (Booths), which began on the fifteenth day of the seventh month when the moon was full. See Lev 23:34; Num 29:12.tn Heb “at the full moon on the day of our festival.” The Hebrew word כֶּסֶה (keseh) is an alternate spelling of כֶּסֶא (keseʾ, “full moon”).
verses.commentary:
81:3 This verse is an admonition to worship God at the appropriate time and place.

- the new moon ‒ Israel's way to mark a new month (BDB 294, i.e., totally dark, cf. Num. 10:10; 28:11-15)

- full moon (BDB 409, i.e., totally bright, its use found only here and Prov. 7:20; it denoted the middle of the month)

- feast day (lists of several annual feast days, cf. Exodus 23 and Leviticus 23)

Surprisingly Sabbaths are not mentioned (cf. 1 Chr. 23:31; 2 Chr. 2:4; Hos. 2:11).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANCIENT NEAR EASTERN CALENDARS

▣ "Blow the trumpet" This instrument (BDB 1051) is mentioned in Exod. 19:16,19, when
Israel prepared herself for YHWH's giving of His laws. Again this is an allusion to the exodus experience.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HORNS USED BY ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FEASTS OF ISRAEL

verses.zh: 因这是为以色列定的律例，是雅各　神的典章。
verses.en: For observing the festival is a requirement for Israel;[NOTE:1] it is an ordinance given by the God of Jacob.
notes: Heb “because a statute for Israel [is] it.”
verses.commentary:
81:4-5 "statute. . .ordinance. . .testimony"
These terms are ways to designate YHWH's revelations to Israel.

- statutes ‒ BDB 349

- ordinance ‒ BDB 1048

- testimony ‒ BDB 730

In context these seem to refer to the revelations about feast days (cf. Exodus 23; Leviticus 23). See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

These laws seem to be the crux of what Ps. 81:5c means.

- Joseph's testimony of his faith in YHWH as he traveled through Egypt

- Moses' testimony as he shared YHWH's predictions of plagues

- the language of the Egyptians, which the Hebrews did not originally understand

- YHWH's laws that Israel rejected (cf. Ps. 81:8,11,13)

- the fearful voice of God on Mt. Sinai (i.e., relates Ps. 81:5c to Ps. 81:6) spoken in Hebrew, which
by this time most Israelites did not understand because they spoke Egyptian. If so, Ps. 81:5c is
more FIRST PERSON MASCULINE SINGULAR, which would denote YHWH.

verses.zh: 他去攻击埃及地的时候，在约瑟中间立此为证。我在那里听见我所不明白的言语：
verses.en: He decreed it as a regulation in Joseph,when he attacked the land of Egypt.[NOTE:1] I heard a voice I did not recognize.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in his going out against the land of Egypt.” This apparently refers to the general time period of Israel’s exodus from Egypt. The LXX reads, “from Egypt,” in which case “Joseph” (see the preceding line) would be the subject of the verb, “when he [Joseph = Israel] left Egypt.”

Heb “a lip I did not know, I heard.” Here the term “lip” probably stands for speech or a voice. Apparently the psalmist speaks here and refers to God’s voice, whose speech is recorded in the following verses.
verses.commentary:
81:5 "a language that I did not know"
This is a literary idiom for Israel's time in Egypt (cf. Ps. 114:1). It is also
used of the invasion and occupation of Canaan by

- Assyria ‒ Deut. 28:49

- Babylon ‒ Jer. 5:15

Many modern translations see Ps. 81:5c as going with 81:6, not
81:5b. If so, it applies to YHWH speaking on Mt. Sinai (i.e., in Hebrew or in
thunder). Israel was afraid of the powerful physical manifestation of YHWH on
Mt. Sinai (cf. Exodus 19-20).

The remaining verses record YHWH speaking (i.e., Ps. 81:6-16).

verses.zh: 神说：我使你的肩得脱重担，你的手放下筐子。
verses.en: It said:[NOTE:1] “I removed the burden from his shoulder;his hands were released from holding the basket.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “It said” are not included in the Hebrew text. They are supplied in the translation for clarification.

I removed the burden. The Lord speaks metaphorically of how he delivered his people from Egyptian bondage. The reference to a basket/burden probably alludes to the hard labor of the Israelites in Egypt, where they had to carry loads of bricks (see Exod 1:14).
verses.commentary:
81:6-10 This strophe is a summary of
all the gracious acts of YHWH in the exodus and wilderness wandering period.
Notice all the FIRST PERSON MASCULINE SINGULAR VERBS! YHWH is
directly addressing His people.

- I relieved (lit. "removed"), Ps. 81:6 ‒ BDB 693, KB 747, Hiphil PERFECT

- I rescued (lit. "delivered"), Ps. 81:7 ‒ BDB 322, KB 321, Piel IMPERFECT with waw

- I answered, Ps. 81:7 ‒ BDB 772, KB 851, Qal IMPERFECT

- I proved, Ps. 81:7 ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT

- I will admonish, Ps. 81:8 ‒ BDB 729, KB 795, Hiphil COHORTATIVE

- I, the Lord, am your God, Ps. 81:10 ‒ covenant language

- I will fill it, Ps. 81:10 ‒ BDB 569, KB 583, Piel IMPERFECT used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

Also notice

- I gave them over to, Ps. 81:12 ‒ BDB 1018, KB 1511, Piel IMPERFECT with
waw (cf. Rom. 1:24,26,28)

- I would quickly subdue, Ps. 81:14

- I would feed you, Ps. 81:16 ‒ BDB 37, KB 46, Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw

- I would satisfy you, Ps. 81:16 ‒ BDB 959, KB 1302, Hiphil IMPERFECT

YHWH speaks from Ps. 81:6 through 16 by means of a priest or prophet.

81:6 This verse refers to the forced labor of the Hebrew slaves (i.e., Exod. 1:8-14).

verses.zh: 你在急难中呼求，我就搭救你；我在雷的隐密处应允你，在米利巴水那里试验你。（细拉）
verses.en: In your distress you called out and I rescued you.I answered you from a dark thundercloud.[NOTE:1] I tested you at the waters of Meribah.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “I answered you in the hidden place of thunder.” This may allude to God’s self-revelation at Mount Sinai, where he appeared in a dark cloud accompanied by thunder (see Exod 19:16).

The name Meribah means “strife.” Two separate but similar incidents at the place called Meribah are recorded in the Pentateuch (Exod 17:1-7; Num 20:1-13). In both cases the Israelites complained about lack of water and the Lord miraculously provided for them.
verses.commentary:
81:7 "You called in trouble and I rescued you" This is an allusion to YHWH's dialog with
Moses in Exod. 3:7-10.

▣ "I answered you in the hiding place of thunder" This seems to allude to Israel's
Mt. Sinai experience (cf. Exod. 19:19; 20:18).

▣ "I proved you at the waters of Meribah" This refers to the Israelites' experience
recorded in Exod. 17:6-7 and Num. 20:13. The AB (pp. 265-266) sees this line as "though I was
provoked by you" (cf. Exod. 17:7; Num. 14:22; 20:24; 27:14; Deut. 33:8). Each of these texts states
that Israel tested God, not God tested Israel.

Deuteronomy 33:8 seems to support the MT of Ps. 81:7c as God
testing the Israelites.

▣ "Selah" See notes at Psalm 3:2.

verses.zh: 我的民哪，你当听，我要劝戒你；以色列啊，甚愿你肯听从我。
verses.en: I said,[NOTE:1] ‘Listen, my people!I will warn[NOTE:2] you.O Israel, if only you would obey me![NOTE:3]
notes: The words “I said” are supplied in the translation for clarification. Verses 8-10 appear to recall what the Lord commanded the generation of Israelites that experienced the events described in v. 7. Note the statement in v. 11, “my people did not listen to me.”
Or perhaps “command.”
The Hebrew particle אִם (ʾim, “if”) and following prefixed verbal form here express a wish (GKC 321 §109.b). Note that the apodosis (the “then” clause of the conditional sentence) is suppressed.
verses.commentary:
81:8 "Hear" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE! It begins a series of references
to Israel's lack of responding appropriately to YHWH's revelation (cf. Neh. 9:34).

- if you would listen ‒ Ps. 81:8

- My people did not listen ‒ Ps. 81:11

- Israel did not obey Me ‒ Ps. 81:11

- Oh that My people would listen to Me ‒ Ps. 81:13

Derek Kidner, in the Tyndale Commentary series (p. 326), thinks
"Hear, O My people" is an allusion to the Shema prayer of Deut. 6:4-6. It
may well be!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

verses.zh: 在你当中，不可有别的神；外邦的神，你也不可下拜。
verses.en: There must be[NOTE:1] no other[NOTE:2] god among you.You must not worship a foreign god.
notes: The imperfect verbal forms in v. 9 have a modal function, expressing what is obligatory.
Heb “different”; “illicit.”
verses.commentary:
81:9 Israel was commanded not to make
or go after foreign gods (cf. Exod. 20:3,23). The Israelites were attracted to
the fertility gods of Canaan. Israel's uniqueness in the ANE was her monotheism,
which allowed for no rivals!

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 1374) asserts that Ps. 81:9-10 are
an allusion to Exod. 20:1-2; Deut. 5:6, but in reverse order.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 我是耶和华―你的　神，曾把你从埃及地领上来；你要大大张口，我就给你充满。
verses.en: I am the Lord, your God,the one who brought you out of the land of Egypt.Open your mouth wide and I will fill it.’
verses.commentary:
81:10 This refers to YHWH's provision
of food and water during the wilderness wandering period.

verses.zh: 无奈，我的民不听我的声音；以色列全不理我。
verses.en: But my people did not obey me;[NOTE:1] Israel did not submit to me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “did not listen to my voice.”
The Hebrew expression אָבָה לִי (ʾavah li) means “submit to me” (see Deut 13:8).
verses.commentary:
81:11-16 This strophe contrasts what
Israel did with what YHWH wanted to do for them.

- Israel's history of rebellion (cf. Ps. 78:17,40; Nehemiah 9; Acts 7)

- did not listen

- did not obey

- had stubborn hearts

- walked in their own devices

- YHWH's reaction

- judgment

(1) gave them over to (cf. Ps. 78:29; Isa. 6:9-10; Rom. 1:24,26,28) the
stubbornness of their hearts, Ps. 81:12; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

(2) gave them over to walk in their own devices, Ps. 81:12; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

(3) those who pretend obedience would suffer eternal loss, Ps. 81:15

- His desire

(1) that they would listen to Him, Ps. 81:13

(2) that they would walk in His ways, Ps. 81:13

- His blessings

(1) subdue their enemies, Ps. 81:14

(2) turn His hand against their adversaries, Ps. 81:14; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

(3) feed them

(a) the finest of the wheat (cf. Deut. 32:14)

(b) honey from the rock (i.e., the best food of the land, cf. Deut. 32:13)

(4) satisfy them

verses.zh: 我便任凭他们心里刚硬，随自己的计谋而行。
verses.en: I gave them over to their stubborn desires;[NOTE:1] they did what seemed right to them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and I sent him away in the stubbornness of their heart.”
Heb “they walked in their counsel.” The prefixed verbal form is either preterite (“walked”) or a customary imperfect (“were walking”).

verses.zh: 甚愿我的民肯听从我，以色列肯行我的道，
verses.en: If only my people would obey me![NOTE:1] If only Israel would keep my commands![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “if only my people were listening to me.” The Hebrew particle לוּ (lu, “if not”) introduces a purely hypothetical or contrary to fact condition (see 2 Sam 18:12).
Heb “[and if only] Israel would walk in my ways.”

verses.zh: 我便速速治服他们的仇敌，反手攻击他们的敌人。
verses.en: Then I would quickly subdue their enemies,and attack[NOTE:1] their adversaries.”
notes: Heb “turn my hand against.” The idiom “turn the hand against” has the nuance of “strike with the hand, attack” (see Isa 1:25; Ezek 38:12; Amos 1:8; Zech 13:7).

verses.zh: 恨耶和华的人必来投降，但他的百姓必永久长存。
verses.en: (May those who hate the Lord[NOTE:1] cower in fear[NOTE:2] before him.May they be permanently humiliated.)[NOTE:3]
notes: “Those who hate the Lord” are also mentioned in 2 Chr 19:2 and Ps 139:21.

See Deut 33:29; Ps 66:3 for other uses of the verb כָּחַשׁ (kakhash) in the sense “cower in fear.” In Ps 18:44 the verb seems to carry the nuance “to be weak; to be powerless” (see also Ps 109:24). The prefixed verbal form is taken as a jussive, parallel to the jussive form in the next line.

The verb form at the beginning of the line is jussive, indicating that this is a prayer. The translation assumes that v. 15 is a parenthetical “curse” offered by the psalmist. Having heard the reference to Israel’s enemies (v. 14), the psalmist inserts this prayer, reminding the Lord that they are God’s enemies as well.tc Heb “and may their time be forever.” The Hebrew term עִתָּם (ʿittam, “their time”) must refer here to the “time” of the demise and humiliation of those who hate the Lord. Some propose an emendation to בַּעֲתָתָם (baʿatatam) or בִּעֻתָם (biʿutam; “their terror”; i.e., “may their terror last forever”), but the omission of bet (ב) in the present Hebrew text is difficult to explain, making the proposed emendation unlikely.
verses.commentary:
81:15 The question is "To whom is this verse directed?"

- Israel's enemies (fits with v. 14)

- unfaithful Israelites? (fits with v. 13). YHWH's blessings and protection conditioned on covenant obedience

▣ "forever" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 他也必拿上好的麦子给他们吃，又拿从磐石出的蜂蜜叫他们饱足。
verses.en: “I would feed Israel the best wheat,[NOTE:1] and would satisfy your appetite[NOTE:2] with honey from the rocky cliffs.”[NOTE:3]
notes: I would feed. After the parenthetical “curse” in v. 15, the Lord’s speech continues here.tn Heb “and he fed him from the best of the wheat.” The Hebrew text has a third person form of the preterite with a vav (ו) consecutive attached. However, it is preferable, in light of the use of the first person in v. 14 and in the next line, to emend the verb to a first person form and understand the vav as conjunctive, continuing the apodosis of the conditional sentence of vv. 13-14. The third masculine singular pronominal suffix refers to Israel, as in v. 6.
Heb “you.” The second person singular pronominal suffix refers to Israel, as in vv. 7-10.
The language in this verse, particularly the references to wheat and honey, is reminiscent of Deut 32:13-14.
verses.commentary:
81:16 This verse is an allusion to the abundance of Canaan (cf. Deut. 8:8).

- for "the finest of the wheat," see Deut. 32:14

- for "honey from the rock," see Deut. 32:13

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in
the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in
interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3).
Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original
author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one
and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There is much debate over whether this relates to the Feast of Booths or Passover.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

- The Targum adds Tishri to Ps. 81:3, which is the month of the Feast of Booths.

- This Psalm obviously refers to the exodus and wilderness experience, so both the
Passover and Feast of Booths fit. I think it is the Feast of Booths or Tabernacles, which
commemorates the wilderness wanderings. JPSOA thinks it refers to the "New Year" liturgy.
The difficulty is that Ps. 81:3 seems to refer to two different dates (i.e., first of the month
and middle of the month).
